title: The Current State of Non-Upright Pedestrian Protection: Fusing Multi-Modal Perception, ISO 26262/SOTIF Standards, and Kinematic Forensics
content: Autonomous and semi-autonomous advanced driver-assistance systems (ADAS) are highly proficient at tracking upright pedestrians under standard environmental conditions. However, individuals in non-upright positions—such as fallen, collapsed, or prostrate vulnerable road users (VRUs)—face a severe safety deficit owing to the classification limits of standard visual-spectrum perception suites. This review examines the intersection of three structural domains required to resolve this edge case: multi-modal multispectral sensor fusion, international automotive safety governance (ISO 26262 and ISO 21448), and post-collision multi-body kinematic reconstruction. By analysing the field’s shift from reactive crash mitigation to predictive temporal perception, this paper provides a high-level blueprint for an integrated safety pipeline capable of transforming unclassified urban anomalies into manageable safety events.
